A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Timer-XL. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments, pre-training evaluations, ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds zero-shot comparisons, forecasting case studies and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The multivariate next-token objective, TimeAttention mask, positional embeddings and forecasting procedure remain unchanged. Clarifying that variable-bias scalars operate per attention head does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Sections 4.4 and E.2 add LOTSA as a substantial pre-training collection alongside UTSD and ERA5-Large, including aggregated UTSD+LOTSA training. Downstream task families remain stable; the additional ETT result blocks concern datasets already listed in v2 Table 8.

E2.justification: Zero-shot comparisons expand beyond Timer to Moirai variants, TimesFM, MOMENT, Chronos and Time-MoE. DLinear joins Figure 3 and UniTST joins Figure 4. Tables 2–4 and 11 also reassign the former Moirai entries to UniTST while retaining their matched scores; the PDFs do not explain whether these were recomputed.

E3.justification: v3 adds LOTSA training configurations and a multi-horizon zero-shot protocol using official checkpoints, each model's maximum input length, and exclusions for pre-training overlap. Additional protocols include ERA5 one-day forecasting across daily-to-yearly lookbacks and 672-to-96 normalization comparisons. Existing supervised splits and settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine prediction quality through showcases (Figures 9–10), encoder-versus-decoder attention behavior (Figure 11), ERA5 context-length sensitivity (Table 14), and normalization dependence on three conventional benchmarks (Table 15). The original embedding ablation is retained as Table 13, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-random-seed standard deviations in Table 9. v3 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation practice, significance testing or repeated-run disclosure.

E6.justification: Tables 6 and 12 add extensive zero-shot results, Table 11 adds three ETT result blocks, and Tables 14–15 add context and normalization findings. Figure 3 revises plotted results; Figure 4 adds UniTST temperature/wind MSEs of 7.356/3.807 against unchanged Timer-XL values of 7.172/3.786. Matched numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the relocated embedding ablation remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A complexity derivations are retained. Permutation-equivariance terminology clarifies the input/output reordering behavior already described in v2; no new mathematical result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central unified-forecasting and TimeAttention contributions remain. The introduction adds an explicit claim of outperforming advanced zero-shot models at comparable model and pre-training scales, while the abstract recasts Timer-XL as a promising foundation-model architecture.

C2.justification: Section E.4 adds explanations involving selective attention versus attention to noisy context and mismatched normalization statistics during autoregression. The earlier inference that decoder-only models better accommodate the embeddings, based on the Moirai comparison, is removed. The limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: Table 10 adds LOTSA training hyperparameters and Moirai configurations, Section E.2 identifies checkpoint-based evaluation, and Table 12 provides a model-checkpoint access link. Section 3.2 clarifies per-head variable biases. Existing implementation documentation largely remains, and the LOTSA training duration is unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to MOMENT, Time-MoE and Deep Sets, removes the Touvron et al. 2021 citation, and shifts the discussion of prior multivariate encoder modeling from Moirai to UniTST. The overall related-work framework remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and several method explanations receive localized rewrites. The embedding-ablation discussion moves to Appendix E.3, and supplementary material gains showcases and thematic subsections. The main section sequence and much existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9–12 and new zero-shot, context-length and normalization tables; expands Tables 10–11; and redraws Figures 3–4 with additional comparators. The original Table 6 moves to Table 13, substantially reorganizing the presentation of experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: v2's zero-shot evidence mainly compared Timer-XL with its predecessor. v3 addresses this important gap with broader foundation-model comparisons and adds context-length, linear-baseline and normalization controls, substantially strengthening evidence for its central claims. Unexplained Moirai-to-UniTST reassignment and inconsistent ECL entries between Tables 6 and 12 weaken reporting reliability, but do not outweigh these gains.
